title: East Sikkim permits explained: PAP, RAP and Nathu La
meta_description: Which permits you need for Gangtok, Tsomgo Lake, Nathu La and the Silk Route: Indian and foreign visitors, documents, days, costs and common mistakes.
summary: Indian citizens need no permit for Gangtok, but need a Protected Area Permit for Tsomgo Lake, Baba Mandir, Nathu La and the Silk Route, arranged through a registered agent. Foreign visitors need a Restricted Area Permit, applied for online, and may visit Tsomgo Lake only. Nathu La is for Indians only, Wednesday to Sunday.

sections.heading: Who needs which permit
paras: Sikkim sits on two international borders, with Tibet (China) to the north and east and Bhutan to the south-east, so parts of East Sikkim are controlled zones. That is the whole reason for the paperwork. The rules differ for Indian citizens and for foreign nationals, and they differ again for each place on the map. We plan dozens of these trips a season, and most permit trouble comes from one of three things: the wrong day for Nathu La, a missing photo ID, or a foreign passport in a group heading for a place foreigners cannot go.

The table below is how we understand the rules in 2026. Permit rules in border areas change with little notice, sometimes overnight after a landslide or a security review, so check current status before you travel. Your hotel or driver in Gangtok will know the latest position by the evening before your trip.

sections.heading: Indian citizens: the Protected Area Permit
paras: An Indian passport holder or Aadhaar holder can drive into Sikkim at Rangpo and spend a week in Gangtok without any permit at all. The permit question starts only when you head east of Gangtok towards the border. Tsomgo Lake (3,753 m), Baba Harbhajan Singh Mandir and Nathu La (4,310 m) all sit inside a protected area, and so does the old trade road beyond Rongli to Zuluk, Nathang and Kupup.

You do not apply for this permit yourself. A registered Gangtok travel agent, or the driver's union through an agent, files it with the Tourism and Civil Aviation Department and the police. The fee for Nathu La has been around ₹200 per person and is usually folded into the vehicle price. For the Silk Route, permits are also issued at Rongli, the small market town where the climb to Zuluk begins, through the local administration and police. Agents in Gangtok handle this too if you start from there.

Since 2025 Sikkim has been moving permits online, with QR-coded passes in trial for Nathu La, Tsomgo, Zuluk and the North. Your agent will tell you whether you need to show one on your phone at the check post. Keep the photo ID you gave for the permit in your pocket, not in the boot.

sections.heading: Nathu La: days, age limits and snow
paras: Nathu La is open to Indian tourists only, on set days. As we understand it, that is Wednesday to Sunday, with the pass closed to visitors on Monday and Tuesday. Agents need your documents a day ahead, often by early afternoon, so a Tuesday arrival in Gangtok can still make a Wednesday trip if you hand in papers on time. The army can shut the pass on any day after heavy snow, a security alert or road damage, and it happens most often between late December and March.

Operators usually will not take children under 5 to Nathu La because of the altitude. Pregnant travellers and anyone with heart or lung trouble should ask a doctor first; the road climbs from 1,650 m to 4,310 m in about three hours, which is a big jump for the body. Check current status before you travel, and if Nathu La closes, most drivers will still run the Tsomgo and Baba Mandir part of the trip at a lower price.

sections.heading: Foreign visitors: RAP first, then Tsomgo
paras: Every foreign national needs a Restricted Area Permit, also called an Inner Line Permit, to enter Sikkim at all. It has been free, valid for 30 days and extendable. For years you could pick one up at the Rangpo check post or at Sikkim Tourism offices in Siliguri, Delhi and Kolkata. In January 2026 the state said paper permits would no longer be issued to foreigners and that applications must go through the e-FRRO portal (indianfrro.gov.in), filed after you reach India and before you enter Sikkim. Check current status before you travel, and give yourself a few days of margin.

Inside Sikkim, the only protected spot in East Sikkim open to foreigners is Tsomgo Lake, on a day permit arranged by a registered agent. Agents usually need at least two foreign travellers to file it, so solo travellers often join a small group. Nathu La, Baba Mandir beyond the lake and the whole Zuluk–Nathang–Kupup Silk Route are closed to foreign passport holders. Overseas Citizens of India (OCI) card holders are treated as foreigners for these permits; ask your agent before you book anything.

sections.heading: Documents and how the agent does it
paras: Pack the paperwork at home so you are not hunting for a photo studio in Gangtok at 6 pm. For a group of four, this list takes about ten minutes to sort and saves a day.

Hand everything over the evening before, or the day before for Nathu La. The agent returns a printed or digital permit with every name on it; check spellings against your ID, because a wrong letter can turn a car back at the check post.
list: Indian citizens: one photo ID per person (Aadhaar, passport, voter ID or driving licence) plus a photocopy.
Two recent passport-size photographs per person, including children.
Children: a school ID or birth certificate copy, since many have no other ID.
Foreign nationals: passport, Indian visa, the approved RAP, and copies of each.
Your Gangtok hotel name and the vehicle number, which the agent adds to the form.
The ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee receipt from your hotel check-in, introduced in 2025; keep it until you leave the state.

sections.heading: North Sikkim and sudden suspensions
paras: Lachung, Lachen, Yumthang and Gurudongmar need a separate protected area permit, again through a Gangtok agent. These permits are the most fragile in the state. In 2025 they were suspended for weeks after landslides in April and June, and the same can happen in any monsoon. If North Sikkim is the heart of your trip, book a plan that can switch: our usual fall-back is an extra East Sikkim day to Tsomgo, Rumtek or Ranka while you wait for the road to reopen.

Never pay a large advance for a North Sikkim package in July or August without a written refund rule for permit suspensions. Check current status before you travel, and again the night before you leave Gangtok.

One more rule catches families out. The protected area permit lists the vehicle as well as the people, so you cannot swap cars halfway or add a cousin at the check post. If someone in your group is unsure about the altitude, decide before the agent files the papers, not at 6 am in the hotel lobby. A late change usually means a fresh application and a lost day, and the money already paid for the car is rarely returned.

sections.heading: Mistakes that cost travellers money
paras: We see the same slips every season. Each one is cheap to avoid and expensive to fix once you are in Gangtok.
list: Booking Nathu La for a Monday or Tuesday. The pass is closed to tourists on those days.
Arriving in Gangtok in the evening and expecting a Nathu La permit for the next morning.
Bringing a foreign friend on a Silk Route or Nathu La trip. They cannot enter, and the whole car may be held up at the check post.
Hiring a car from Siliguri for Tsomgo. Only Gangtok-registered tourist vehicles are allowed on the permit routes, so you pay twice.
Forgetting photographs. A studio near MG Marg can print them, but that eats an evening.
Treating a permit as a guarantee. Snow or a landslide can close a road after your permit is issued; ask about refunds before paying.

faqs.q: Do Indians need a permit to visit Gangtok
faqs.a: No. Indian citizens need no permit to enter Sikkim or to stay in Gangtok, Rumtek or Ranka. You only need a Protected Area Permit for Tsomgo Lake, Baba Mandir, Nathu La and the Silk Route beyond Rongli. Carry a photo ID anyway, since hotels record it at check-in and collect the ₹50 Sikkim tourist fee introduced in 2025. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do I get a Nathu La permit
faqs.a: Through a registered Gangtok travel agent or your hotel's agent; you cannot apply alone. Give them one photo ID copy and two passport photos per person, usually a day before the trip. The permit fee has been around ₹200 per person and is often included in the vehicle price. Nathu La is open to Indian tourists Wednesday to Sunday. Check current status before you travel.

No. Nathu La is open only to Indian citizens, and that has been the rule for many years. Foreign nationals with a valid Restricted Area Permit can visit Tsomgo Lake on a day permit through a registered agent, usually in a group of at least two. The Silk Route villages of Zuluk, Nathang and Kupup are also closed to foreigners. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How do foreigners get the Sikkim RAP in 2026
faqs.a: Online. In January 2026 Sikkim said foreign visitors must apply for the Restricted Area Permit through the e-FRRO portal at indianfrro.gov.in, after arriving in India and before entering Sikkim, and that paper permits would no longer be issued at the border. The RAP has been free and valid for 30 days. Apply a few days early and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Nathu La open on Monday
faqs.a: No. As we understand the rule, Nathu La is closed to tourists on Monday and Tuesday and open Wednesday to Sunday. Even on open days the army can close the pass after snow or for security reasons, most often from late December to March. If that happens, drivers usually still run Tsomgo Lake and Baba Mandir at a lower fare. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Can children go to Nathu La
faqs.a: Operators usually will not take children under 5 to Nathu La, because the pass is 4,310 m high and the climb from Gangtok takes only about three hours. Older children can go with a photo ID or school ID and two photographs. Keep them warm, give them water, and turn back if they show headache, vomiting or unusual sleepiness, which are early signs of altitude sickness.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for Zuluk and the Silk Route
faqs.a: Yes, if you are Indian; foreigners cannot go. The Protected Area Permit for Zuluk, Nathang and Kupup is issued at Rongli or arranged by a Gangtok agent, and you need photo ID and two photographs per person. Aritar and Rhenock, lower down, need no permit. Your driver must carry the permit at every check post. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How much does a Tsomgo Lake permit cost
faqs.a: The permit itself is cheap and agents usually include it in the vehicle hire, so most people never see a separate bill. Expect to pay ₹4,500–6,500 for a Gangtok-registered car to Tsomgo and Baba Mandir with the permit handled, or ₹800–1,300 for a seat in a shared vehicle, indicative 2026. Ask the agent to confirm in writing that the permit is included.

faqs.q: Are North Sikkim permits open now
faqs.a: It depends on the week. North Sikkim permits for Lachung, Lachen and Gurudongmar were suspended for weeks after landslides in April and June 2025, and suspensions can happen in any monsoon or after snow. Ask your agent the evening before you leave Gangtok, and only pay a large advance if there is a written refund rule. Check current status before you travel.
